# Threat model

## Security objective

Pixel should be highly capable without allowing untrusted email, Calendar, social,
web, machine output, or downloaded content to acquire credentials or execution
authority. A compromised model-facing process should be limited to submitting requests
that an external policy compiler can independently reject, constrain, or hold for
human approval.

## Trust zones

| Zone | Trusted for | Never trusted for |
|---|---|---|
| Pixel model and gateway | user dialogue, typed request creation | source truth, credential custody, execution policy, approvals |
| Local control service | strict public settings/status projection, opt-in sanitized Frontier review projection, three fixed local actions, and disabled-by-default maintenance/containment actions | credential display, generic execution, deployment activation, broker approval, backup restore, broker resume |
| Local control browser page | owner interaction with projected state, sanitized capsules, and exact action previews | secret custody, arbitrary paths/commands, approval authority, proof that the host, browser extension set, or owner account is uncompromised |
| Source Broker | API credential custody and deterministic projection | authorizing actions from content |
| Web Courier | bounded public rendering under egress policy | authenticated browsing or instructions |
| Operations Broker | policy compilation, target identity, execution, audit | treating command output as authority |
| Frontier Broker | egress classification, redaction, plans, budgets, provider custody | treating remote advice as authority |
| Dedicated runner transport | forced SSH grammar and typed root helper routing | running untrusted workloads |
| Dedicated runner workload | isolated tests, builds, and unprivileged helpers | SSH key custody or any sudo authority |
| Human operator | client authorization and exact high-risk approval | safely approving without inspecting the plan |

## Primary attack paths and controls

| Attack | Principal controls |
|---|---|
| Email or page tells Pixel to run a command | raw source separation; untrusted labels; operations policy compiles independently |
| Model submits arbitrary argv | plugin accepts names/parameters; broker resolves fixed argv and anchored patterns |
| Model requests excessive standing authority | only operator CLI can issue leases; exact selectors, parameter constraints, TTL, budgets, audit, and single-use IDs |
| Production policy accidentally grants autonomy | production and every change-tier automatic action require an external temporary lease |
| Prompt injection requests raw shell | shell becomes a break-glass plan; external exact-hash approval is mandatory |
| Output tells Pixel to approve a follow-up | output signals, redaction, explicit non-authority boundary; approval unavailable to Pixel |
| Gateway compromise steals SSH/OAuth keys | distinct users; `ProtectHome`; private directories unreadable; no credential paths in gateway environment |
| Legacy or future OpenClaw config key silently widens capability | renderer builds the complete top-level/default-agent config from an explicit allowlist and preserves only typed message, HTTP-endpoint, model-timeout, and approved extension/channel compatibility fields |
| Old config smuggles a plugin, host bind, provider secret, or unsandboxed agent | renderer reconstructs agents, providers, tools, plugins, memory, and Docker policy from explicit onboarding inputs |
| Local control is exposed through LAN bind, DNS rebinding, or cross-site request | exact `127.0.0.1` binding; strict Host and same-origin mutation checks; random HttpOnly SameSite cookie; no CORS; restrictive content policy |
| Browser input smuggles a credential, path, command, or widened setting | exact additional-properties-false onboarding schema; no credential/path/command fields; fixed typed validators; advanced private fields are preserved but never returned |
| Confirmed local action changes or replays before execution | SHA-256-bound five-minute preview; exact onboarding, private-policy, and generated-deployment revisions; immutable private configure snapshot; atomic single-use claim; one service instance; restart recovery |
| Local action floods disk, memory, CPU, or process lifetime | request/rate/pending/result/log ceilings; bounded pipe reader; fixed timeout; process-group termination; private retention cleanup |
| Corrupt local result or metric exfiltrates text through status | status schema emits only fixed enums, validated timestamps, bounded counters, and fixed boundary text; action IDs, paths, logs, prompts, and arbitrary record fields are omitted |
| Another local user/process reads sanitized reviews through loopback | session cookie alone is insufficient; review endpoint requires a separate random per-process bearer delivered only in the terminal URL fragment, removed from visible history state, never returned by HTTP, and compared in constant time |
| Corrupt Frontier result smuggles arbitrary data into the review page | view disabled by default; fixed result filename/version/state; exact capsule schema, instructions, metadata, counters, cost mode, and canonical hash revalidation; allowlisted reconstruction; no-follow/single-link/size/count/response bounds; text-only DOM rendering |
| Malicious page, extension, or unattended process approves a protected plan | browser exposes no approval action or generic execution; the source, Operations, and ordinary Frontier wrappers require a controlling terminal, pinned system path, fresh password-backed administrator authentication, complete protected-object display, and an unpredictable hash-bound typed phrase; cached authentication is invalidated before and after; broker rechecks the exact plan/capsule/policy/request/expiry/cancellation/budget before execution |
| Browser triggers maintenance or restores authority without prior operator policy | optional actions are disabled by default and bind an opaque no-follow private-policy revision; backup path/recipient remain private; update cannot prepare/activate; pause is one-way and resume/restore stay outside the browser |
| Fake, replayed, mixed, ambiguous, or tampered release reaches update intake | independently provisioned OpenSSH allowed-signers trust, exact publisher identity and signature namespace, raw-envelope signature, fixed filenames, exact archive/SBOM/provenance hashes and sizes, exactly one supported compatibility/source record, required versioned audit/table members, and SBOM/provenance cross-binding |
| Release evidence creates a self-reference, omits required evidence, or hides code changed after qualification | signed envelope separately binds the exact packaged commit/tree and qualified functional commit; signer proves clean exact HEAD, ancestry, and an exact three-file ordinary-file evidence delta; equal, unknown, non-ancestor, incomplete, deleted, or functional deltas fail closed |
| Release archive claims a trusted source commit but carries different files | before key use, signer compares the complete archive file/directory set, normalized modes, and every source byte to the exact Git tree; only the separately hashed generated SBOM addition is accepted |
| Malicious update archive exploits intake before approval | no extraction or candidate execution; no-follow single-link bounded inputs; one exact top-level release root; traversal, duplicate, link, special, privileged, oversized, or excessive members fail closed |
| Envelope or private-key path changes during signing | signer validates and reads each single-link input once, copies the reviewed bytes into a private temporary directory, signs only those copies, and creates the detached signature without overwrite |
| Staged update is mixed, altered, replayed, or left partial | deployment and staging locks; owner-only real directories/files; deterministic version-plus-envelope candidate ID; exact receipt and artifact revalidation; no overwrite; bounded retention; safe exact-file interrupted-copy recovery; forward-only floor; no extraction/execution/activation authority |
| Candidate exploits compatibility rehearsal or touches production | no-follow regular-file-only normalized extraction into private staging; path/count/member/unpacked/disk bounds; atomic no-replace publication; sanitized parser environment; fixed pinned Node/Bash syntax modes and Python AST-only compile; no candidate program invocation, network, credential/private-state read, active-deployment path, or activation authority |
| Ambient installed skill injects instructions into Pixel | per-agent `agentSkills` is an explicit replacement allowlist and defaults to empty |
| Untrusted customization pack executes in the gateway | gateway adapter is a byte-exact Pixel template; schema and signed tree reject arbitrary or added gateway files; install and enable are separate confirmed steps |
| Local limb worker gains ambient host/network/credential authority | v1 authority is offline and credential-free; signed systemd template uses a dedicated non-login identity, private network, strict filesystem, empty capabilities, and one projection-only write path shared only through an enabled gateway-user ACL |
| Pack is changed, replaced, or publisher-swapped after review | canonical tree lock and detached Ed25519 verification; activation revalidates the installed receipt; upgrades require the active publisher and explicit migration edge |
| Signed Local policy claims authority or another limb's tool | exact observe-only/untrusted/no-raw-content schema; tools must be a subset of the containing signed limb; retention cannot exceed the limb boundary |
| Signed Operations pack smuggles shell, private targets, or production autonomy | namespaced actions; fixed Pixel helper argv only; target placeholder only; no production/change standing grant; explicit private onboarding mapping plus per-file hash |
| Signed Frontier pack widens egress or creates a generic prompt | supported typed tasks only; configure composes restrictions against the base policy and rejects enablement, classifications, token limits, rehydration, or tools that widen it |
| Policy receipt is swapped after limb activation | no-follow bounded read, exact file SHA-256, path confinement below the active extension, signed manifest declaration, version/tree-lock provenance, and full extension-tree digest before apply |
| Untrusted content asks Pixel to inspect or message another session | one managed agent; session list/history/send visibility fixed to the current spawn tree; unrelated exact keys are gateway-forbidden |
| Two allowlisted direct-message senders share private context | per-account/channel/peer DM session scope plus a dedicated per-client gateway |
| Control API is exposed or unauthenticated | service forces loopback binding and token auth; runtime listener/auth probes are release gates |
| Gateway changes a Calendar proposal after review | broker-owned protected snapshot; external exact SHA-256 approval; result hash verification |
| Prompt injection attempts a direct Calendar write | deterministic broker policy permits only private no-attendee creates or one ETag-bound time-only reschedule; deletes, people, content, and recurrence fail closed |
| Target impersonation | strict preexisting host-key pin plus expected-hostname verification and cache |
| Broker SSH key or hostile runner workload is misused | root-owned `pixel-ops-transport` key/home, forced command, no arbitrary shell, fixed helper grammar, descriptor-based cwd confinement, and a separate non-login `pixel-runner` workload identity with no sudo rule |
| Path or symlink escape | absolute allowed roots; secure spool opens; regular-file checks; no-follow receiver handles |
| Download reaches internal service or escapes reviewed provenance | HTTPS-only transport, public-IP validation, DNS pinning, redirect source-domain enforcement, TLS hostname check, optional required content hash |
| Download smuggles executable | quarantine, byte cap, SHA-256, mode without execute bits, separate verified transfer |
| Job floods output or never exits | bounded readers, hard timeout, process-group cancellation, workflow abort propagation |
| Approval is replayed or plan changes | unique job ID, single-use approval, TTL, canonical plan SHA-256 recheck |
| Pixel or injected source content forwards private data to Codex | two typed task classes only; local-first contract; declared data categories; never-egress/secret/quarantine rejection; supported identifier replacement |
| Sanitized Frontier plan changes after review | canonical capsule, policy, provider, model, budget, expiry, and authority are bound into one exact plan hash; policy drift and replay fail closed |
| Codex uses tools to inspect the host or request more data | empty ephemeral home, ignored user config/rules, shell/web/browser/computer/image-generation/apps/plugins/hooks/goals/multi-agent disabled, read-only sandbox, offline tool-manifest qualification, no capsule paths, structured output, hostile-output rejection |
| Frontier API key is exposed to Pixel | separate system identity and root-owned broker-group-readable credential; no policy/credential path in gateway environment or sandbox mounts |
| ChatGPT Codex auth cache is exposed, replaced, or widened | broker-owned mode-`0700` auth directory; single-link mode-`0600` JSON cache; root-owned non-writable parent; descriptor-bound validation before startup and every provider run; no gateway path or projected credential data |
| Paid spillover loops or runs away | required local-attempt/reason receipt, content-free rolling usage projection, token/job budgets, per-grant bounds, observed usage receipts, timeout/cancel, and failure circuits |
| A model name, size claim, or stale backend is treated as proof of capability | content-free empirical receipt binds exact model artifact, backend, prompt, tool schema, test corpus, expiry, tested context/output envelope, and observed usage source; substitution or estimated usage cannot enter a qualified route |
| A worker repeats equivalent calls, oscillates, or rewrites event history to appear productive | controller-owned calls use a checkpoint-bound preflight watchdog; the opaque OMP RPC stream separately session-keys canonical arguments plus completed results, stops repeated successes/failures and exact A/B oscillation, and persists only a content-free count/head receipt. The ephemeral key prevents low-entropy output guessing from the retained head. OMP's stream is observational because its tool starts internally before the host event arrives, so disposable isolation and hard budgets remain mandatory |
| Cancellation races first launch or hides a live worker behind a terminal parent | lease consumption and revocation compete for the same immutable per-lease slot, so exactly one wins; only an exact revoked plan may be admitted to record an iteration-zero, zero-use child with no execution evidence; a consumed lease requires supervised cleanup before parent cancellation; stale, substituted, pre-custody, or ambiguous evidence fails closed |
| Cleanup fails, an orphan may remain, or recovery cannot prove which resources belong to the attempt | the exact consumed claim and checkpoint derive cleanup-only authority; unproven removal records `cleanup-failed` with conservative usage and can only retry the same cleanup; unsafe or ambiguous inspection records terminal `recovery-inconclusive`; neither state can launch work, and a successful retry preserves the prior charge rather than double-counting |
| Several long goals oversubscribe one host, starve a peer, repeat a completed turn after a crash, skip an interrupted owner, or silently outlive stale capacity evidence | the disabled fleet foundation binds every exact goal/controller/job set and selected goal-checkpoint head to its truthful peak worker envelope and admits one durable round-robin turn; the private bridge derives eligibility from authoritative ledgers, settlement rotates past the selected goal, and a crash leaves that turn exclusively active until exact recovery. An already-advanced head is settled without a second cycle. The rendered cadence serializes live capacity refresh, cycle, and cleanup under one fleet lock and refuses startup beside installed legacy per-goal units. Hash-confirmed activation revalidates exact live contracts and every durable ledger. The controller binds one immutable probe policy and one evidence genesis; maximum-24-hour observations append in a predecessor-bound chain without configuration drift. The read-only Linux probe rejects inactive, unlimited, or under-reserved shared units, and each record subtracts explicit system and shared-service CPU, memory, disposable disk, and retention ceilings. Registration drift, understated resources, expired evidence, chain gap/rollback/tampering, host-identity change, malformed receipts, cleanup failure, and forged settlement fail closed. Deterministic eight-day restart/fairness/renewal coverage passes. A credential-free event-horizon probe drives repeated independent branches and verified convergence, kills fresh controllers after every durable child transition, and verifies exact recovery without replay in each supported-host lane. Promotion requires its maximum exact-source 64-milestone, 84-edge, 256-crash, 385-process form. A separate networkless UTC-hourly systemd soak can still test delayed lease refresh, append-only invocation custody, and controlled reboot behavior over 48 hours, but it is optional appliance evidence: elapsed time never counts as useful work or promotion evidence. |
| Local input admission follows a link, snapshots its own output, accepts a changing tree, creates an extraction collision, exhausts disk, or misbinds a private dataset | owner names each absolute canonical source directory in a strict private selection; every source component resolves without symlinks; only single-link regular files and real directories enter a bounded deterministic ustar stream; entry/file/extracted/archive ceilings apply before publication; source identities and directory metadata are rechecked; output ancestry and safe-projection collisions fail closed. Catalogs omit source paths, control files remain inert, and Data Lab files require canonical unique IDs, matching extensions, non-inert exact relative paths, raw byte hashes, and isolated replay verification |
| Compacted context smuggles authority, crosses clients, or resumes a stale lease | private hash-bound capsule binds exact plan/checkpoint/classification and lineage; text is untrusted; forks use new jobs and cannot reuse leases, approvals, credentials, or completion claims or lower classification |
| A context-session review is replayed against changed private files, concurrent applies create divergent forks, listing leaks content, or interrupted removal leaves a recoverable live copy hidden | review hash binds the private state root plus exact plan, checkpoint, context, parent, classification, and lifetime; all inputs are bounded owner-only no-follow single-link files; an append-only apply claim makes concurrent creation converge on one capsule; ordinary receipts and inventory views contain only bounded metadata; content requires an explicit trusted-terminal `show`; removal uses exact-hash hard-link custody, a content-free tombstone, bounded monotonic recovery, and never claims storage-media or backup erasure |
| An MCP adapter expands its tool surface, inherits secrets, replays a claim, smuggles data in text, silently downgrades classification, or survives cancellation | digest-bound pack and exact schema discovery; recent passing health; a separately issued expiring grant and checkpoint-bound watchdog decision; empty host environment; networkless read-only least-privilege container; atomic claim plus durable execution-start tombstone; exactly one call; structured-output/text equality with raw text discarded; preserved classification; bounded frames, stderr, runtime, processes, memory, CPU, and disposable workspace. Cleanup custody binds the exact image, job, claim, container, and optional volume; ownership is inspected before removal and absence is independently proven. Only structured output crosses the live caller boundary, while content-free terminal evidence stores no arguments or result. Recovery can finish cleanup or publication but never replay the tool |
| A worker hand-builds a capability authorization, substitutes a checkpoint or pack, widens resources/classification/effects, forges event history, or waits for a timer to reset a stalled loop | the pure controller revalidates the exact plan, consumed single-use lease, consumption tombstone, running checkpoint, signed pack hash/tree, private policy, job authorization, request, signed input schema, and trusted event-chain head on every decision. Profile, generic job tools, disposable-write state, classifications, session count, grant lifetime, compute/storage ceilings, and watchdog limits can only narrow. Repeated/failing/oscillating/no-progress events return a stop decision with no grant regardless of elapsed time; clocks only expire stale authority. |
| Two controllers race one capability request, a crash loses transient output, an uncertain launch is retried, a response appears without an event, or stopped work keeps queuing | one owner-private single-flight claim transfers the exact request into durable custody; append-only hash-chained phase records bind its authorization, checkpoint, decision, grant, runtime receipt, event, and response without content. The `launching` record is a conservative replay horizon. Recovery can finish cleanup and use already-staged job-private output, but absent output settles an uncertainty event and response without execution. Event and response publication are exact-once and restart-idempotent; one terminal stop record rejects later enqueue. Aggregate runtime and retained-input/output ceilings cover the full authorized session count. |
| An OMP worker discovers an ambient capability, collides with a builtin, substitutes a catalog/schema, races event heads, accepts a stale response, or retries after an ambiguous published request | the controller derives one fresh content-addressed catalog from the exact job authorization and signed pack; deterministic `pixel_cap_*` aliases and collision rejection isolate the namespace; the trusted static extension passes through the exact signed raw schemas, serializes calls, and advances the event head only from a response bound to the request, authorization, checkpoint, classification, active lifetime, schema, and digest. The private queue has an exact shape and no ambient registration. Any post-publication ambiguity closes the session. The extension has no network, credentials, process launch, grant, external-effect, or completion authority and remains unrouted until the complete profile lifecycle is qualified. |
| A capability declaration or image is substituted, signed by an untrusted publisher, raced against revocation/removal, linked into private state, oversized during extraction, partially installed or removed by a crash, replayed after removal, or mistaken for an enabled tool | descriptor-bound single-link reads; canonical Ed25519 namespace and exact signer identity; independently provisioned current allowed-signers root; private atomic no-replace declaration installation; exact installed shape and re-verification; incomplete residue and trust revocation fail closed. Image admission uses an empty credential-free Docker configuration, an already-local canonical repository manifest digest, separately signed local Docker image ID and Linux platform, `--pull never`, exact-safe-environment and metadata checks, a never-started hardened container, bounded strict single-file tar extraction, exact executable hash/size, and forced-remove plus independent inspect/list absence proof after every create attempt. One schema-bound exact-pack single-writer record serializes admission, revocation, and removal. Revocation is exact-review bound and retains the unowned host image. Pack removal atomically transfers custody, persists separate pre-delete custody proof, exposes intent/move/custody/finalization recovery state, writes a no-residue tombstone, and rejects same-version reinstall. Declaration and image admission remain disabled and every tool/data/network/effect/completion authority flag remains false |
| A health check becomes a hidden tool invocation, receives client data, enables an untrusted capability, leaks failure text, races another pack mutation, or leaves an orphaned container | the explicit confirmed disabled health operation has no grant and performs only exact MCP discovery and signed-schema tool listing with an empty input surface; it never invokes a tool or registers the capability. Exact-pack operation custody precedes launch, a sterile networkless read-only container receives no workspace or client data, runtime and resources are bounded, and forced removal plus inspect/list absence proof is mandatory. Chained content-free receipts retain only fixed state, counts, hashes, and timing; three consecutive failures quarantine the signed version. Crash recovery resumes only the exact cleanup or staged publication, while concurrent operations converge on one winner and every other pack mutation remains blocked |
| Private knowledge leaks across clients, becomes ambient authority, returns an irrelevant recent item, is replayed after state change, remains after retention, or is silently corrupted | external 256-bit key with per-source authenticated encryption; owner/client/classification partition; keyed lexical term index; explicit exact ingestion consent; single-use job/checkpoint query at an exact vault head; deterministic minimum relevance and no fallback; cited untrusted output with no authority; exact deletion tombstone, retention purge, deep audit, and crash recovery |
| A historical backup resurrects deleted private knowledge or restores obsolete key wrapping | Deep Work quiescence; separately staged restore; active vault as authoritative deletion ledger; exact tombstone conflict/content checks; ciphertext removal before activation; rotation to the current external key; final deep audit; atomic swap with automatic rollback. Backup refuses any vault key inside captured roots |
| Deep Work status leaks content, smuggles authority, presents stale state as current, understates budget use, or uses an identifier as a tracking channel | controller emits fixed enums and bounded counters under an exact schema; job/event identities become keyed display handles and are removed by the second validator; at most one current session is marked and both validators prove settled-plus-current use and `remaining = limit - used`; privacy and all snapshot-control flags are exact false constants; linked/corrupt/unknown/incoherent state fails closed; snapshots older than two minutes render offline; the browser uses text-only DOM construction. The separate opt-in pause accepts no caller path or free text, binds a private config revision into exact confirmation, executes only against a single-use owner-private byte snapshot, stops future scheduling only, and leaves resume/cancel terminal-only |
| Guided browser authoring leaks private paths/hashes, accepts an unadmitted input, downgrades classification, races policy/catalog drift, fills storage, or becomes an execution surface | owner-private fixed-path configuration is supplied only at process launch and gated by both private policy and the process-lifetime review token; catalog IDs become keyed opaque handles and only generic kind/classification/size/dataset summaries cross the endpoint; strict request/config/projection contracts reject unknown fields and paths; serial dependencies are server-derived; private research and classification downgrade fail closed; exact confirmation binds current config, policy, catalog, and translated brief; execution invokes only the fixed inert drafter with single-use private brief, policy, and catalog byte snapshots; bounded retention and atomic no-replace publication apply; no admission, compile, lease, stage, schedule, run, egress, scope, or completion route exists |
| Guided draft assembly substitutes reviewed work, misbinds final controller paths, publishes a partial controller, smuggles an extra file, or becomes implicit activation | terminal confirmation binds the canonical draft review; the complete declaration, jobs, per-child input manifests, review projections, and hashes are revalidated from owner-private single-link files; a private off-path transaction builds both bundles while controller paths bind the final destination; only a complete exact manifest is atomically published; unexpected files, links, overlap, races, and interruption fail closed; assembly creates no plan, lease, ledger, custody, timer, service, worker, network request, external effect, or completion claim |
| Deep Work spillover exports a private request, tenant identity, document identity, raw source body, or credential | separate disabled policy and task switches; required local-attempt receipt; exact classification/category and content-hash validation; never-egress rejection; allowlisted language metadata; secret and opaque-token denial; declared/common identifier replacement; synthetic document IDs; capsule-only future provider boundary |
| A crafted placeholder causes ambiguous or attacker-controlled rehydration | all input containing the reserved marker is rejected; compiler alone issues typed sequential placeholders; plan inventory must equal the exact capsule; replacement map and private random commitment nonce remain local; future output may refer only to issued placeholders and still requires local validation |
| ChatGPT subscription access is confused with separately billed API use | authentication and billing shapes are mutually constrained; ChatGPT plans carry no dollar ceiling or API claim; API-key plans require dated rates and a worst-case local cost ceiling; neither compile path reads a credential or invokes the provider |
| A green Codex preview, mock, fake-CLI, or local image test is presented as completed remote work | preview constants and local image evidence state that no provider or real credential was used; output is schema/hash-bound; preview and mock receipts deny verification/completion authority; the fake qualifier is single-use and empty-auth; no test path can create external provider provenance |
| A mock or fake-CLI test is mistaken for a live Codex turn or silently gains network authority | mock authorization/storage require explicit test flags and `test-mock`; source is fixed `mock` and provider state `not-invoked`; the isolated adapter instead requires `external-signed-mfa`; the fake qualifier is unwired, inherits no credentials/proxies, and cannot enter either execution source |
| Browser state, a forged assertion, or replay grants Codex spillover | no browser approval route; exact private policy pins issuer, audience, Ed25519 public-key fingerprint, password plus allowed second factors, authentication and evidence ages; assertion binds the complete plan/provider/billing and typed-challenge hash; evidence tombstone is atomically created before authorization and one concurrent caller wins; synthetic verification does not claim a production identity provider exists |
| Credential custody leaks a token, cache, account, or filesystem location | broker-private absolute path is a deployment input, never policy; real private directory and bounded single-link regular-file checks; strict UTF-8 and auth-mode shape; API file identity is frozen; ChatGPT rotation is revalidated; content-free receipts expose no path/content/hash; opaque handles have no reflectable state; credentials stay outside arguments, environment, plans, UI, and receipts |
| CLI injection, ambient config, diagnostics, malformed events, floods, or orphan processes escape the qualifier | absolute executable/bootstrap paths and direct argv without a shell; no task data in argv; ignored config/rules and strict deny config; sterile home/temp/workspace and environment; bounded strict-UTF-8 ordered JSONL plus exact final file and usage; generic errors; live byte monitors; timeout/abort; POSIX process-group or Windows process-tree kill; one-use runtime cleanup |
| The isolated Codex runner reads the host, inherits configuration, bypasses its proxy, or substitutes a weaker image | exact local image ID, platform, labels, Codex/native/entrypoint hashes, network membership, proxy identity/policy, user, mounts, environment, resources, ports, devices, and hardening are re-inspected before credential projection; the runner is non-root, read-only, capability-free, no-new-privileges, socket-free, bounded, disposable, and attached only to the broker-owned internal network |
| DNS rebinding, worker DNS exfiltration, proxy smuggling, an IP literal, stale policy, or a permissive proxy turns the provider route into general egress | worker DNS disabled and proxy addressed by inspected private IP; exact canonical CONNECT grammar; one exact hostname and port 443; no proxy auth/plain HTTP/IP literal/unknown headers; whole-answer-set public-address validation; connection to the vetted IP; startup policy-hash binding; end-to-end TLS; bounded headers/concurrency/bytes/connect/idle; no body logging; pinned proxy image and inspectable policy hash |
| A credential crosses through arguments, environment, mounts, logs, or a reusable container | credential and task are separate length-framed stdin fields; an ephemeral private Codex home receives only the required auth form; API login uses child stdin; ChatGPT refresh is validated before atomic replacement; generic errors, no body logs, forced container removal, and credential-directory cleanup apply on every terminal path |
| Timeout evidence is returned while an isolated credential-bearing container is still cleaning up | executor aborts the isolated adapter and waits a bounded cleanup grace; the adapter force-removes the exact named container, proves no matching container remains, removes its runtime, and withholds success plus auth-cache refresh if removal cannot be verified |
| Authorization is raced, replayed, or reused after a timeout/crash | exact authorization and plan are revalidated before an atomic claim-directory create; the durable claim is written before adapter entry; one concurrent caller wins; any existing or partial claim burns the authorization and requires recovery rather than retry |
| Provider output invents placeholders, targets another document, smuggles a secret, widens schema, or is rehydrated outside the private boundary | exact canonical JSON and hash-bound output schema; task and synthetic target checks; issued-placeholder set equality; visible-normalized text and secret/opaque-token denial; bounded usage/bytes; local-only exact replacement; owner-only output; content-free no-authority receipt |
| Local model misclassifies sufficient, retryable, or context-blocked work | broker validates versioned outcome/reason coherence and deterministic attempt ceilings; local-only/retry/context create no plan or provider call; safety/security reasons force approval before any spillover |
| Exact duplicate jobs spend twice | cache key binds capsule/policy/provider/auth/model/output contract; cross-process transaction serializes lookup and execution; approval-time recheck occurs before approval consumption |
| Cache entry is substituted, widened, stale, or used to bypass approval | private no-follow single-link bounded file; exact binding and output validation on every read; TTL/entry cap; confidential/approval/forced-review/quality-circuit work is ineligible |
| Cost estimate is missing, forged, or treated as billing truth | provider policy selects unavailable/subscription/metered; only dated operator-supplied metered rates produce currency estimates; rolling ceiling is checked before execution; actual usage stays separately recorded |
| Live qualification is used to export data or smuggle a credential | no prompt/file/URL/credential input; exact fixed public/structural synthetic request; additional-properties-false consent schema; broker recompiles and compares the complete request before approval |
| Live qualification confuses ChatGPT access with API billing | exact auth-mode binding; ChatGPT requires plan-or-credits acknowledgment and no dollar claim; API requires separate billing acknowledgment, fresh metered policy evidence, and a worst-case micro-dollar ceiling |
| Live confirmation is replayed or retried after an uncertain provider turn | short-lived authorization hash is consumed once; private immutable claim binds job/plan/policy/caps; exact approval is single-use; rerun returns terminal evidence or an inconclusive receipt without another execution |
| Remote advice becomes an unverified final answer | plugin requires local critique, exact finding partition, verification count, verdict, and final local composition; broker accepts only a content-free receipt bound to the exact successful result |
| Quality regresses while automatic spillover continues | content-free improved/unchanged/regressed/unusable receipts feed a bounded-auto downgrade circuit and disable cache reuse; operator approval remains available |
| Concurrent changes race | singleton broker lock, cross-process authority lock, persistent budgets, target exclusivity, and dependency graph validation |
| Artifact changes between hash and installation | root helper copies exact hashed regular file into root-owned verified quarantine before fixed install command |
| Managed change fails verification | helper performs bounded automatic rollback and reports both outcomes; pause/revoke do not interrupt the recovery transaction |
| Attacker supplies a forged or malicious private backup | age decryption is not treated as authenticity; detached Ed25519 signature is checked against a separately trusted signer, then paths, types, links, sizes, duplicates, and manifest roots are audited before isolated staging |
| Restore fails after replacing some roots | services stop first; same-parent transactional swaps retain every prior root; failed verification rolls all roots back and restarts prior services |
| Operator needs an emergency stop | pause blocks new execution and stops read/staging jobs; reason and resume are audited |
| Disabled capability remains reachable | per-limb plugin/service omission plus explicit tool denies and clean-room matrix test |

## Deliberate residual risks

- A model can still request any operation that the private policy allows. Policy quality
  and target isolation remain critical.
- A permitted read command can expose sensitive information in its output. Actions must
  select narrow, redactable data rather than general logs or environment dumps.
- A dedicated runner is a software boundary on the target, not a hardware air gap.
  Kernel or helper vulnerabilities can cross it.
- An operator can approve a dangerous exact plan. The system provides inspection,
  binding, expiry, and auditability; it cannot replace judgment.
- Human approval trusts the non-root deployment owner's terminal, administrator secret,
  and sudo/PAM policy. A compromised owner session, terminal emulator, root, or kernel is
  outside this boundary. An uncatchable process termination can defer Pixel's final
  timestamp removal until the operating system's configured sudo timeout; keep that
  timeout short and do not share the approval terminal.
- A correctly scoped lease deliberately delegates real capability for its lifetime. The
  broker contains it but cannot determine whether the operator's business intent was
  wise. Use minimum duration and budgets, then revoke it.
- The Source Broker's deterministic sanitizer can miss novel semantic attacks. Its
  stronger protection is removal of credentials and direct actuators from Pixel, not
  perfect content classification.
- The Frontier privacy compiler can miss names, novel identifiers, semantic business
  secrets, or deliberately obfuscated material. Confidential approval and data-owner
  classification remain necessary; regulated records and raw source bodies are denied.
- Frontier mode is not a physical air gap. Permitted capsules and provider metadata are
  processed under the configured OpenAI account's current data-handling terms, region,
  retention, and organizational controls.
- The Deep Work Codex sanitizer is also not a semantic secrecy oracle. It can miss novel,
  obfuscated, encoded, or context-dependent disclosures. Structural-only mode, explicit
  owner classification, default disablement, exact preview, and a separate live approval
  reduce risk but cannot turn an approved network transmission into a physical air gap.
- Local attempt outcomes and post-integration quality labels are local-model assessments,
  not independently measured truth. They can reduce provider use or downgrade automation,
  but never widen authority or bypass approval. Operators must investigate repeated
  regressions rather than treating the circuit as a quality oracle.
- A process already running as the Frontier Broker identity can alter its own cache and
  integration files. File ownership isolates the gateway and other unprivileged users;
  it does not defend against compromise of the broker identity, root, or kernel.
- The pinned Codex executable, pinned proxy image, container runtime, DNS resolver, and host
  kernel are trusted computing-base components. Tool disabling and the exact-host proxy
  constrain the model/network surface, not a malicious executable, compromised runtime,
  compromised allowed provider endpoint, or kernel escape.
- Frontier output limits and required usage receipts are validated and accounted locally,
  but the Codex CLI path has no server-side hard output-token switch. One failed or
  over-limit attempt, including provider-added input overhead or CLI-managed retries,
  can consume more tokens than reserved; provider project budgets remain the outer
  circuit.
- A compromised gateway can fill its writable Frontier request/cancel spool before the
  broker rejects or drains it. Use a monitored, quota-limited filesystem or equivalent
  service-level storage limits; broker authority and private data remain separately owned.
- The model endpoint and OpenClaw runtime remain supply-chain and confidentiality
  dependencies. Keep them private, pinned, patched, and backed up according to client
  policy.

## Release and incident rule

Safety and capability are both release gates. A build fails if it blocks the documented
safe workflow, silently loses progress/cancellation, exposes credentials, accepts an
identity change, follows untrusted instructions, or allows a disabled limb. Use only
fake canaries and disposable artifacts in adversarial tests. On a changed SSH identity,
credential exposure, policy-integrity failure, or unexpected tool call: quarantine the
limb, preserve bounded audit evidence, rotate affected authority, and re-enroll through
an independently verified channel.

## Legacy clean-migration threat surface and rollback boundary

The 3.2.2 to 4.2 path is a terminal-only clean migration, not an in-place update. The
primary attack surface is a tool, operator error, or attacker that mistakes it for an
in-place 3.2.2 update, weakens the forward policy, mutates a live path during rehearsal,
or swaps the bound plan/backup/rehearsal/restore evidence. The model treats these as
release-failing controls:

- **No in-place update claim.** `migrate-legacy-clean` and the release manifest keep
  `qualificationMode=forward` and `minimumUpgradablePixel=4.0.0`. A manifest that weakens
  these, or a plan/rehearsal/completion receipt that records a non-forward policy or a
  non-3.2.2/non-4.2.0 version pair, fails schema and policy validation.
- **No automated activation.** bootstrap, apply, replace-restore, and rollback are never
  invoked by the tool. `finalize` only requires the authenticated backup and a private 0600
  restore receipt, recomputes the backup SHA-256, confirms the active release pointer is
  exactly `releases/4.2.0`, runs `./pixel verify --expected-install-dir ABSOLUTE` (which
  fails closed unless the trusted configuration's `PIXEL_INSTALL_DIR` resolves exactly to
  that safe non-root path), separately requires the attestation at the same directory, and
  strictly validates the fresh runtime attestation plus a single clean, current Git source
  identity bound across every phase.
- **Fail-closed evidence binding.** Plan, rehearsal, and completion receipts require exact
  artifacts and recomputed content hashes; stale plan/rehearsal hashes, mismatched backup
  SHA-256, a stale/forged/wrong-source restore receipt, an unavailable or contradictory
  runtime attestation, or a restore receipt that did not pass are all rejected. The old
  minimal `{status,mode}` restore artifact is rejected.
- **Path and identity safety.** Every receipt is written owner-only (parent `0700`, file
  `0600`), atomically, with no-overwrite, outside the source repository, and is content-free.
  Rehearsal is allowed only into an explicit new non-live root and is refused for any live
  path. Installed-version inspection does not follow unsafe links and rejects escapes.
- **Rollback boundary is the backup.** There is no in-place rollback from a 3.2.2 source.
  If a clean 4.2 deployment must be abandoned, the legacy environment survives only as the
  authenticated backup; it must be restored onto a fresh compatible host, never over a live
  4.2 install. The completion receipt is terminal handoff evidence, not a reversible
  in-place transition.
